title: Minimum Division Operations to Make Array Non Decreasing
summary: Given an integer array nums, you can divide any element by its greatest proper divisor any number of times.
statement: Given an integer array nums, you can divide any element by its greatest proper divisor any number of times. Determine the least number of operations needed to ensure the array is non-decreasing. If it's impossible, return -1.
constraints: One operation divides a value by its greatest proper divisor, changing a composite value to its smallest prime factor.
Return the fewest operations making nums nondecreasing, or -1 when impossible.
hints: A useful operation maps a composite number directly to its smallest prime factor; repeating cannot reduce that prime.
Precompute smallest prime factors, then scan right to left so the fixed suffix supplies the allowed upper bound.
When values[i] exceeds its neighbor, replace it once; fail if it remains too large.
Each inversion forces that element’s only useful reduction, and the sieve supplies it in constant time during the scan.
editorial: Each inversion forces that element’s only useful reduction, and the sieve supplies it in constant time during the scan.

tests.explanation: Twenty-five becomes 5 after division by its greatest proper divisor 5, producing [5,7].
A prime seven cannot be reduced by the operation, so the final inversion cannot be repaired.
